clue.text: Victorian poet has pigs drinking in Northern stream

indicators.note: pigs drinking in something take it inside them, so the pigs word holds the stream word

parts.note: swine are pigs
a burn is a stream in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: A Victorian versifier shares his northern stream with a herd of thirsty pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word. Algernon Charles Swinburne was a Victorian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Charles Swinburne was an English poet of the Victorian era, an example of the type named.

clue.text: Small bouquet's sent up for network controller

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a posy is a small bouquet of flowers, and the 's here supplies an S

explanation.surface: A little bunch of flowers is posted up to the person running the network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses POSYS (posy's) in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sysop, short for system operator, is the person who runs a computer system or network.

clue.text: A. Lincoln organised school discipline to be fair

indicators.note: organised means arranged in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a science is a branch of study taught at school

explanation.surface: Abraham Lincoln set up a strict schooling regime in the name of fairness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges A LINCOLN into IN ALL CON.
explanation.definitionFit: In all conscience is an idiom meaning honestly or by any fair standard, so it can replace 'to be fair'.

clue.text: Typically male bachelor, fine wearing flowery wreaths on horse

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree

indicators.note: the wreaths are worn around the word for fine, enclosing it

parts.note: leis are Hawaiian garlands of flowers
OK means fine
H is slang for heroin, called horse, and the drug's abbreviation

explanation.surface: A single man, decked out in floral garlands, rides a horse in a very masculine way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word placing H after the rest in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Blokeish means behaving in the hearty manner thought typical of men, a bloke being British slang for a man.

clue.text: Place for improving crude material on best clothes

parts.note: re means on or concerning
finery is one's best, showiest clothes

explanation.surface: A place where rough fabric is turned into the smartest clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' suggests rough, but it is crude oil, which a refinery processes.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is an industrial plant where crude oil or other raw material is purified.

clue.text: Mathematician from London campus in Muslim festival

indicators.note: the campus goes inside the word for the festival

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival, as in Eid al-Fitr
UCL is University College London

explanation.surface: A mathematician from a London college attends a Muslim festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek mathematician famous for his Elements of geometry.

clue.text: Noah's son in turn takes one chapter in Old Testament book

indicators.note: one piece takes the others into its middle, so they go inside it
turned round, so the son's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Ham was one of the three sons of Noah in Genesis
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A son of Noah features, with one chapter, in a book of the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' reverses HAM to MAH; 'takes' puts IC inside it after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Micah is one of the minor prophetic books of the Old Testament, so it is an example of such a book.

clue.text: Not quite what Oliver asked for, hugging a certain listless person

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around something, so it goes inside
not quite means one letter short at the end

parts.note: Oliver Twist famously asked for more gruel in Dickens's novel
one as in 'a certain person', one man

explanation.surface: Oliver Twist's famous request, slightly short, embraces someone with no energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts the last letter of Oliver Twist's request, leaving MOR; 'hugging' wraps that round the word for a certain one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooner is someone who moons about, wandering idly and listlessly.

clue.text: Source of numerous channels with viable selection sorted out

indicators.note: sorted out means arranged differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A workable choice of channels has been put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Cable television delivers many channels down a cable, so it is a source of numerous channels.

clue.text: Initially, Capricorn or Pisces in house was in the ascendant in this?

definitions.text: Initially, Capricorn or Pisces in house was in the ascendant in this?

indicators.note: the initials go inside the house and rising words

parts.note: rose means was rising, gaining power

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Astrology talk: star signs, houses and the ascendant all appear in a reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Houses and the ascendant are astrology terms, so the whole clue also describes the chart itself; 'in' places the initials inside the rising word.
explanation.definitionFit: A horoscope is an astrological chart of planets in signs and houses, with the sign in the ascendant.

clue.text: Isolate mutating of fleas

indicators.note: mutating means changing form, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: A biologist watches fleas mutate and wants them kept apart from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutating' rearranges OF FLEAS into SEAL OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To seal off an area is to close it so nothing gets in or out, which isolates it.

clue.text: Clubs fight, excluding iron lever

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs
a row is a quarrel or fight
bar as a preposition means except, excluding

explanation.surface: A golf club's squabble ends with someone being barred, or perhaps brandishing an iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is a heavy iron bar used as a lever to prise things apart.

clue.text: Sign of life that's enjoyed by vegans?

definitions.meaning: a heartbeat felt at the wrist shows someone is alive
beans, lentils and peas are edible seeds central to a vegan diet

explanation.surface: Something both proves you are alive and goes down well with vegans.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the beat of the heart felt in an artery, and pulses are also edible legume seeds like lentils.

clue.text: Injury to the back, ending for woman's mum

indicators.note: sending a word to the back means reading it backwards

parts.note: a lesion is an injury or wound
-ess is the suffix that makes a female form, as in lioness or actress

explanation.surface: A woman's mother has hurt her back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the back' reverses LESION to NOISEL. 'mum' looks like a mother but means silent, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mum means keeping silent and making no sound at all.

clue.text: Longs to suppress, initially imprisoning agitator

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding another piece inside
initially means take the first letter of each of the words to and suppress

parts.note: a rouser stirs people up, an agitator

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to silence a troublemaker by locking him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longs' looks like a verb meaning yearns, but is a noun for long trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Longs is an informal name for long trousers, as opposed to shorts.

clue.text: Capped increase relating to false charges?

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or trump it
up means an increase, as in a price going up

explanation.surface: A wage cap and a rise are being argued over in a dispute about charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' looks like prices, but here it means accusations.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumped-up describes accusations that are invented or fabricated, such as false charges.

clue.text: Contents of some more diplomatic communication?

indicators.note: the contents of the phrase are the letters held inside it

explanation.surface: A request for further diplomatic notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo, short for memorandum, is a written note, and a memorandum is also a formal diplomatic communication.

clue.text: Island wood whose roots may be waterlogged

definitions.text: Island wood whose roots may be waterlogged

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea
a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: Trees on an island stand with their roots in water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the tree: mangroves grow in tidal water.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangroves are tropical trees growing in coastal swamps, with roots often submerged by the tide.

clue.text: I act badly, in actual truth

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for actual

parts.note: very as an adjective means actual, as in 'the very man'

indicators.note: badly done means messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor admits his poor acting is the real truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns I ACT into ACIT, which 'in' places inside the word for actual.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracity is truthfulness, conformity to the facts, so it serves as a synonym of truth.

clue.text: Bear aloft leader of Republicans in the States …

indicators.note: the leader goes inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: USA, the United States of America

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Republican leader in America is a political bear in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Ursa (Major or Minor) is a bear constellation, so it is aloft in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Major and Ursa Minor are the Great and Little Bear constellations, seen high in the night sky.

clue.text: … whose uncle gets pardon before me too

parts.note: continuing from the previous clue, the States' uncle is Uncle Sam
eh? is said when asking someone to repeat themselves, like pardon?
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: The clue continues the previous one, where an American uncle asks for a repeat and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 17: the States' uncle is Uncle Sam.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'same here' is an informal way of agreeing that you feel likewise, just as 'me too' does.

clue.text: To rear, emulate Bambi's mother, perhaps

parts.note: to emulate is to try to be like, so here be
Bambi's mother was a deer, and a hind is a female deer

explanation.surface: To raise young, copy Bambi's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' looks like the verb to raise, but means the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind means at or towards the rear, the back of something.

clue.text: Maybe hope to struggle out of terrible rut

indicators.note: the struggle word sits outside the rearranged letters

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Hope helps someone fight their way out of a dreadful rut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' turns the rut into RTU, held by the struggle word ('out of'). Hope is one of the three theological virtues with faith and charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is one of the three theological virtues, with faith and charity, so it is an example of a virtue.

clue.text: Maybe use a 10, sounding knell for Fight Club venue?

indicators.note: sounding means a word is said aloud and spelt as another that sounds the same

parts.note: 10 across is a crowbar, and using one is to prise something open
to knell is to toll or ring a bell

explanation.surface: A crowbar is wielded as a bell tolls, in the run-up to a bout at a fight club.
explanation.walkthrough: PRISE sounds like PRIZE. A prize ring is a boxing ring for prizefights.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize ring is the roped ring in which prizefighters box, so fitting as the venue for a fight club.

clue.text: Prejudice against the grey and silver is minute

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiny prejudice exists against those with grey and silver hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is discrimination against people because of their age, and 'the grey' are older people.

clue.text: Insect appearing round first of November or December, say

indicators.note: the insect goes round the letter

parts.note: a moth is an insect

indicators.note: the first of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An insect appears around the start of November or December.
explanation.definitionFit: December is an example of a month, one of the twelve in the calendar year.

clue.text: Occasional driller stinted unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters land in an unforeseen order

explanation.surface: Someone who only drills now and then has been surprisingly sparing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist drills teeth only now and then, when a filling is needed, a witty description of the job.

clue.text: View round wing

parts.note: O is round in shape
a pinion is the outer part of a bird's wing, or a wing in poetry

explanation.surface: A view all round the wing of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is the view a person holds on a matter, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Argue for pawn to go first

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
to lead is to go first

explanation.surface: In chess, someone argues that a pawn should be moved first.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to argue earnestly in favour of something, as a lawyer pleads a case.

clue.text: Wholly English, extremely fashionable church

parts.note: very means extremely
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A church that is entirely English and very much in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Every inch is an idiom meaning completely, entirely, as in 'every inch a gentleman'.
